programme.desc: Tonight, Maeve visits the crayfishermen off Geraldton and tastes just how good a 'cray on the barbie' can be. Guy drops in on Melbourne chef Maurizio Esposito to learn the secrets of his delicious crayfish gnocchi recipe. Maeve then seeks out the best pizza and Guy discovers artichokes. Also, Sicilian-born gelato-makers explain why Italian gelato is so good.

programme.title: America The Bountiful
programme.desc: We'll explore the storied history of the oyster in modern day South Carolina.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet With Justine Schofield
programme.desc: Learn how to make the The Original 'One Bowl' chocolate cake, a twice roasted duck with delicious orange nam jim and some mouth-watering steamed pork buns.

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw
programme.desc: It's Refugee Week on The Cook Up, and Adam, refugee advocate Monika Kollaras and award-winning author Alice Pung are here to share some dinner lessons.

programme.title: Great Chocolate Showdown
programme.desc: The home bakers delve into fruit jellies and bejewel a chocolate sculpture in pate de fruits.

programme.title: Bring A Plate
programme.desc: Nimi serves up her favorite vegetarian Punjabi dish, Poori-Chole. Even though some guests can't eat spicy food, Nimi shares how to enjoy the dish using yoghurt and pickles so everyone can enjoy it.

programme.title: Great Chocolate Showdown
programme.desc: With immunity off the table, the top six bakers pair up to build a magnificent meringue tower.

programme.title: Please Eat Slowly Bitesize
programme.desc: Learn how to make mouth-watering Yee Sang. Victor has a few tricks for slicing the perfect julienne at home, as well as some presentation tips to make your salad a showstopper.

programme.title: Destination Flavour Down Under
programme.desc: Expect the unexpected on this tour of the Northern Territory. Starting off at the heart of Australia, Uluru, Adam visits a Vietnamese garden oasis in the middle of the desert, calls in on a butcher who fishes for perch in his backyard, and meets an outback chef who makes him a special set of knives with the steel forge in his backyard. He finds the prospect of butchering a crocodile quite confronting during this adventure, but soon embraces the task and scores a fillet to use in a prawn and crocodile laksa. During a day out on the magnificent waters of Nitmiluk Gorge, Adam nets a barramundi, which he cooks up at a breathtaking spot in front of Edith Falls.

programme.title: Flat Out Food
programme.desc: Jenn visits an organic grain farmer, a baker, and a whiskey maker to learn about the various uses of wheat.

programme.title: On Country Kitchen
programme.desc: Arriving in Berrima, Brigid takes the boys through the kitchen garden attached to her restaurant, The Loch. At Maple Ridge Farm, Derek and Mark help in milking the goats at the dairy and back in Jervis bay, Joel and Adrian catch and cook up some abalone burgers for a beach fire and feed with the little ones. Atop Cambewarra mountain, Joel tells the story in language of the black cockatoo overlooking the picturesque NSW landscape.

programme.title: Rachael Ray's Meals In Minutes
programme.desc: Rachael shows us how to make a beautiful, white, quick cooking ragu sauce that she'll serve over ribbony pappardelle pasta cooked al dente style.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt explores Noosa Farmers Market with a vegan recipe, silken tofu with chilli and spring onion. Mike hits the road with Mann About Town, David Mann, whipping up pork cutlets, nashi pear, and Kohlrabi slaw. Pastry Chef Kay-Lene Tan and Executive Chef Adam D'Sylva engage in a sweet versus savory battle. Laura closes with BBQ lamb cutlets with smokey gremolata.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Life can be hard, so let Lidia's simple recipes provide some relief & inspiration to feel healthy.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.sub-title: Nectar Of The Mayan Gods, The
programme.desc: Pati is in the magic town of Mani to learn about something sacred to the Mayans: bees and honey. She makes sweet lime roasted chicken with broccolini.

programme.title: Silvia's Italian Masterclass
programme.desc: A celebration of the Italian Sunday tradition, where Nonna's table brings together family, tradition, and irresistible flavours from slow-cooked sugo to crispy festive sweets.

programme.title: Italian Food Safari
programme.desc: Guy discovers a huge family vegetable and herb garden in Melbourne’s suburbs which provides meals and even the wine to drink with it. Maeve finds prosciutto in Adelaide, and is cooked pasta and beans by Armando Percuoco in his country estate. In Melbourne, cheesemaker Giorgio Linguanti takes Guy back to his childhood, while Loretta Sartori cooks a spectacular ricotta cake.

programme.title: America The Bountiful
programme.desc: Chiles are the backbone of Southwestern cuisine and are celebrated throughout the region.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet With Justine Schofield
programme.desc: Justine demonstrates how to make tasty marinara balls in tomato sauce and some fillo chocolate croissants. Adam Liaw makes his sweet almond pudding with poached apricots.

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw
programme.desc: It's Refugee Week on The Cook Up. Fashion designer Anjilla Seddeqi and Refugee Council Ambassador Lizzy Kuoth join Adam to share the food that is always on their tables.

programme.title: Luca's Key Ingredient
programme.desc: This season, Luca dives even deeper into the soul of Italian cuisine, blending heritage and creativity to showcase how everyday ingredients can be transformed into extraordinary dishes.

programme.title: Mary Berry's Cook & Share
programme.desc: Mary Berry starts the Edinburgh marathon & surprises runners at the finish line with chocolate treats. She also visits the Botanic gardens, sharing recipes that showcase its produce.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching For Mexico
programme.desc: Eva Longoria shows us around her adopted second hometown, Mexico City. This is where she met her husband, Pepe, and where they love to spend time with their son, Santi. She takes us on her daily ritual to a local bakery where she devours a delicious, freshly baked concha. Then, Eva heads to the historic centre to meet up with food writer Gabriela Renteria where they sample the 'lifeblood' of Mexico City - tacos.

programme.title: Destination Flavour Down Under Bitesize
programme.sub-title: Destination Flavour Down Under Bitesize Series 1 Ep 1

programme.title: Come Dine With Me: The Professionals
programme.desc: The competition has headed to Edinburgh where first to host are front of house Matthew and chef Yaw from Bundits. They are hoping to impress their guests Buumba and Mario of Riverlife and Frazer and Jon of Piper’s Rest with a variety of colourful Asian street food.

programme.title: Torres Strait At Home
programme.sub-title: Wattleseed Damper With Golden Syrup Butter
programme.desc: Wattleseed are one of Nornie's top five favourite ingredients. She uses them here to make a childhood staple, damper, which is wrapped in banana leaves before baking for added fragrance.

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw
programme.desc: It's Refugee Week on The Cook Up. Fashion designer Anjilla Seddeqi and Refugee Council Ambassador Lizzy Kuoth join Adam to share the food that is always on their tables.

programme.title: Cheese Slices
programme.desc: Squeaky, salty haloumi is one of the world’s best-loved grilled cheeses. However most of it is now mass produced using cows milk. Will travels to the island of Cyprus to see how traditional Haloumi is still made from a mixture of goat’s and ewe’s milk. After discovering a fresh, mild whey cheese called Anari, he then visits one of the last farm producers still making Haloumi the old fashioned way from raw milk. Finally, Will checks out some unusual ways to cook this delicious cheese in his home town of Melbourne.

He hears how architect Basil Spence won a competition to build it anew and tours the breathtakingly modernist concrete structure built alongside the medieval ruin.

programme.title: Rambo: First Blood Part II

programme.title: Monsieur Verdoux
programme.desc: Monsieur Verdoux (Charlie Chaplin) is a dapper Parisian family man who loses his job as a bank clerk. In order to support his wife and child, he devises a plan to woo and marry rich widows under a variety of aliases, then murder them for their money. His scheme works until his 14th victim, the loud-mouthed Annabella Bonheur (Martha Raye), proves impossible to kill.

programme.title: Discovering Film: Ian Mckellen

Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. Long married to a successfully driven but inattentive movie producer (Alec Baldwin), she finds herself taking a car trip from Cannes to Paris with a business associate of her husband (Arnaud Viard). What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

programme.title: Like Water For Chocolate

When Pedro marries her sister, Tita throws herself into her cooking and discovers she can transfer her emotions through the food she prepares, infecting all who eat it with her intense heartbreak. Directed by Alsonso Arau and stars Lumi Cavazos and Pedro Muzquiz.

programme.title: The Sitting Duck

In order to support his wife and child, he devises a plan to woo and marry rich widows under a variety of aliases, then murder them for their money. His scheme works until his 14th victim, the loud-mouthed Annabella Bonheur (Martha Raye), proves impossible to kill.

programme.title: Discovering Film: Ian Mckellen

Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. Long married to a successfully driven but inattentive movie producer (Alec Baldwin), she finds herself taking a car trip from Cannes to Paris with a business associate of her husband (Arnaud Viard). What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

programme.title: Like Water For Chocolate

When Pedro marries her sister, Tita throws herself into her cooking and discovers she can transfer her emotions through the food she prepares, infecting all who eat it with her intense heartbreak. Directed by Alsonso Arau and stars Lumi Cavazos and Pedro Muzquiz.

programme.title: The Sitting Duck

Will visits several of the exciting new farmstead cheese producers, including Uplands Cheese Company, before meeting Willi Lehner at Bleu Mont Dairy to see how he ripens cheese in an underground cave. He catches up with Coffin Bay oyster farmer Lester Marshall, and local fisherman Neil Evans. In order to support his wife and child, he devises a plan to woo and marry rich widows under a variety of aliases, then murder them for their money. His scheme works until his 14th victim, the loud-mouthed Annabella Bonheur (Martha Raye), proves impossible to kill.

Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. Long married to a successfully driven but inattentive movie producer (Alec Baldwin), she finds herself taking a car trip from Cannes to Paris with a business associate of her husband (Arnaud Viard). What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

When Pedro marries her sister, Tita throws herself into her cooking and discovers she can transfer her emotions through the food she prepares, infecting all who eat it with her intense heartbreak. Directed by Alsonso Arau and stars Lumi Cavazos and Pedro Muzquiz.

programme.title: Rambo: First Blood Part II

programme.title: Monsieur Verdoux
programme.desc: Monsieur Verdoux (Charlie Chaplin) is a dapper Parisian family man who loses his job as a bank clerk. In order to support his wife and child, he devises a plan to woo and marry rich widows under a variety of aliases, then murder them for their money. His scheme works until his 14th victim, the loud-mouthed Annabella Bonheur (Martha Raye), proves impossible to kill.

programme.title: Discovering Film: Ian Mckellen
programme.desc: Some of the biggest film stars in history rose to fame during the `golden age' of Hollywood, in the early and mid-20th century. We profile some of these stars who became household names.

programme.title: Bonjour Anne: Paris Can Wait
programme.desc: Eleanor Coppola’s narrative directorial and screenwriting debut stars Academy Award nominee Diane Lane as a Hollywood producer’s wife who unexpectedly takes a trip through France, which reawakens her sense of self and her joie de vivre. Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. Long married to a successfully driven but inattentive movie producer (Alec Baldwin), she finds herself taking a car trip from Cannes to Paris with a business associate of her husband (Arnaud Viard). What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

programme.title: Like Water For Chocolate
programme.desc: In a Mexican border town around 1910, Tita falls passionately in love with Pedro, but her controlling mother forbids her from marrying him. When Pedro marries her sister, Tita throws herself into her cooking and discovers she can transfer her emotions through the food she prepares, infecting all who eat it with her intense heartbreak. Directed by Alsonso Arau and stars Lumi Cavazos and Pedro Muzquiz.

programme.title: The Sitting Duck
programme.desc: In 2012, the head union representative of a French multinational nuclear powerhouse becomes a whistle-blower. Maureen Kearney fights government ministers to bring the scandal to light.

programme.title: Princess Caraboo
programme.desc: In the early 19th century, a mysterious young woman speaking a strange language shows up in an English village. There she is taken in by a family of haughty aristocrats who assume she is a foreign princess. Directed by Michael Austin and stars Phoebe Cates, Jim Broadbent and Wendy Hughes.

programme.title: Angel And The Badman
programme.desc: Quirt Evans, an all round bad guy, is nursed back to health and sought after by Penelope Worth, a Quaker girl. He eventually finds himself having to choose between his world and the world Penelope lives in.

programme.title: Where The Money Is
programme.desc: Nurse Carol and her loyal husband Wayne discover that retired bank robber Henry is faking his condition. Together, they plan a heist - but as tensions rise, the robbery takes unexpected turns.

programme.title: Shaft
programme.desc: Cool private eye John Shaft is hired by a crime lord to find and retrieve his kidnapped daughter. Starring Richard Roundtree.

programme.title: Bones Of Crows
programme.desc: Bones of Crows is Aline's journey from child to matriarch, a moving multi-generational epic of resilience, survival and the pursuit of justice.

programme.title: Book Of Love

programme.desc: The upper Midwest state is famous for its ‘cheese heads’ and proudly declares itself America’s Dairyland because it produces more cheese than any other state in the USA. But since the 1950s, most of the original traditional cheese types have been replaced by bland and predictable mass-produced Swiss and Cheddar. Will visits several of the exciting new farmstead cheese producers, including Uplands Cheese Company, before meeting Willi Lehner at Bleu Mont Dairy to see how he ripens cheese in an underground cave. Finally, Will heads for the hills to look at Hidden Springs Creamery, where a new organic ewe’s milk cheese is being made with the help of local Amish farmers.

programme.title: Kitchen Glow Up

programme.title: Destination Flavour Down Under
programme.desc: Back in his home state of South Australia, Adam revisits the Eyre Peninsular where he spent many summer holidays of his youth. Starting in the southern Flinders Ranges, he makes his way south from Port Augusta towards Port Lincoln, stopping in at his father’s old hometown of Whyalla for a trip down memory lane. He catches up with Coffin Bay oyster farmer Lester Marshall, and local fisherman Neil Evans. After reeling in the famed King George whiting, he takes his catch inland to the snow-white landscape of a salt lake where he cooks up his version of classic fish and chips using King George whiting.

Also, Sicilian-born gelato-makers explain why Italian gelato is so good.

programme.title: Destination Flavour Down Under
programme.desc: Expect the unexpected on this tour of the Northern Territory. Starting off at the heart of Australia, Uluru, Adam visits a Vietnamese garden oasis in the middle of the desert, calls in on a butcher who fishes for perch in his backyard, and meets an outback chef who makes him a special set of knives with the steel forge in his backyard. He finds the prospect of butchering a crocodile quite confronting during this adventure, but soon embraces the task and scores a fillet to use in a prawn and crocodile laksa. During a day out on the magnificent waters of Nitmiluk Gorge, Adam nets a barramundi, which he cooks up at a breathtaking spot in front of Edith Falls.

programme.title: Flat Out Food
